terms.ATS: Applicant Tracking System — Automated software used by employers to parse resumes, filter mandatory competencies, and rank candidate fit against job requirements.
terms.BM25: Best Matching 25 — A probabilistic ranking function used in information retrieval and search engines to score relevance between search keywords and text documents.
terms.Verbatim Citation: An exact character-for-character snippet extracted directly from the candidate's resume, proving that a required skill is present in the text without LLM hallucination.
terms.OR-group: A requirement group where satisfying ANY one of several interchangeable skills (such as React OR Vue OR Angular) meets the employer's bar without penalizing missing alternatives.
terms.Score Ledger: A transparent line-item mathematical breakdown showing exact points earned, max weight, calculation formula, and inputs for every scoring factor in the evaluation.
terms.Evidence Depth: A measure of how strongly a skill is supported in your bullet points (e.g. simple mention vs quantifiable production usage vs multi-project architectural leadership).
terms.Parse Quality: An assessment of how cleanly automated ATS software can parse your resume's sections, dates, contact details, and text formatting without corruption.
terms.Keyword Stuffing: The bad practice of listing dozens of skill keywords in an isolated skills list without demonstrating their practical application in work experience or projects.
terms.Transferable Skills: Competencies acquired in one domain or tech stack (e.g. C++ multi-threading or SQL database tuning) that readily apply to another target domain or framework.
terms.Typical Bar: The expected hiring criteria and proof standard (projects, scale metrics, system ownership, on-call experience) typically expected for candidates at a given seniority tier.
